policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV moves straight from 'against Israel:' into the quotation in v.3 with no 'saying'; the ASV renders λέγων explicitly where it stands, so the absence of any such word marks the shorter reading.

ASV has 'they have killed thy prophets, they have digged down thine altars' with no conjunction before the altars clause, though it does render the following κἀγώ as 'and I am left alone'; the added καί is not represented.
ASV ends v.6 at 'otherwise grace is no more grace' and has nothing answering the further clause about works no longer being work.
καθώς and καθάπερ are both rendered 'according as'; the ASV wording cannot tell them apart and no note is mapped here.
ASV opens 'But I speak to you that are Gentiles' — the adversative 'But' answers δέ, not the causal γάρ, which the ASV renders 'for'.
ASV 'Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of Gentiles' renders the inferential particle with 'then'; the omitting reading leaves nothing for that word.

ASV text reads 'partaker with them of the root of the fatness of the olive tree' without 'and', and the mapped textual_variant note assigns 'of the root and of the fatness' to many ancient authorities — i.e. to the margin, not to the text.
ὑψηλὰ φρόνει and the compound ὑψηλοφρόνει both yield 'be not highminded'; the ASV wording does not distinguish the two spellings.
ASV states the apodosis flatly, 'neither will he spare thee'; the reading with μήπως would give a cautionary 'lest he also not spare thee', which the ASV does not have.
Nominative ἀποτομία and accusative ἀποτομίαν are both rendered by the bare noun 'severity' in 'toward them that fell, severity'; case is invisible in the English.
ASV reads 'but toward thee, God's goodness'; the genitive θεοῦ is rendered, and the competing reading has χρηστότητα alone with nothing to answer 'God's'.
Present ἐπιμένῃς and aorist ἐπιμείνῃς are both rendered 'if thou continue'; the ASV does not mark the aspect.
Present ἐπιμένωσι and aorist ἐπιμείνωσιν are both rendered 'if they continue not'; the ASV does not mark the aspect.
The two readings differ only in the order of ἐστιν and ὁ θεός; both give 'God is able', and Greek word order is not recoverable from the ASV.
ASV 'wise in your own conceits' fits the bare dative ἑαυτοῖς and equally the readings with ἐν or παρά; the English 'in your own' does not tell which preposition, if any, stood there.
ASV reads 'the Deliverer; He shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob' with no 'and' before the second clause of the quotation, where the added καί would be rendered.
ASV reads 'For as ye in time past were disobedient to God'; there is no 'also' answering the added καί, which the ASV renders elsewhere in the passage ('they also', 'thou also').

ASV renders 'now' twice in the verse — 'have these also now been disobedient' and 'they also may now obtain mercy' — so both occurrences of νῦν stood in the text the ASV translated; the omitting reading leaves one of them unrepresented.
